items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had never met Dave or Daniel before the studio... Dave had a tune. That’s basically it. We just played.

ctx.x: For Enja. No, that one wasn’t leased. That was their – that was the company. That was their suggestion, to do that. I had never met Dave or Daniel before the studio. So there was no rehearsal or anything with that. I brought some music, and Dave had a tune. That’s basically it. We just played. It was interesting, because it made me play differently, playing with those two guys. It brought out a different thing for me. That record actually won, in Paris, an award. So yeah, that was definitely a lot of fun to do.
Then, also on Enja Records, right after that, the next year, What If?, with Wallace Roney, John Stubblefield, Cecil McBee, and Victor Lewis, one of my favorite drummers.
